ActionEffect.description: An Aktionseffekt of a block (see BaseBlock.actionEffects): something the block does while it is there, to move to another place or to draw attention to itself. Like an Aufbau/Abbau it is an event of the page's graph (`block-action:<blockId>:<id>`, with its trigger stored in PageTimeline.triggers) - only what it does lives here. The player carries it out with the CSS properties `translate` and `rotate` (so they do not meet the `transform` of the block's own rotation or of its Aufbau/Abbau), and what a "move" has done stays: the block is where it went, and the next effect starts from there.

easing.description: "move" only: a CSS timing function (`ease-in-out`, `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`, ...) for how fast it goes along the way. Absent: "ease-in-out".

path.description: "move" only: the way the block takes, as points in percent of the slide's width (x) and height (y), measured from where the block is when the effect starts - not necessarily where it was put on the slide. The last point is where it ends; a curve runs through all of them. Absent or empty: it does not move (it may still turn).

rotation.description: "move" only: how many degrees it turns on the way - clockwise when positive, counterclockwise when negative, and not limited.

ActionEffectType.description: What an Aktionseffekt does to its block between its Aufbau and its Abbau: it moves to a point (and may turn on the way), it shakes once, or it blinks once.

ArrowBlock.description: An arrow: a curve through its waypoints (two or more; the first and last are its ends), with an arrowhead at either end if wanted. The block's box is the box around the waypoints (the editor keeps them in step - see core/document/arrow.ts), so moving, rotating, scaling and the entrance/exit effects work on it like on any other block. Drawn by runtime/arrowGeometry.js, the same code in the editor and the player.

actionEffects.description: What the block does between its Aufbau and its Abbau (see ActionEffect) - in the order they were made; when they happen is a matter of the page's graph. Absent: none (a module saved before they existed).

entranceEffect.description: How this block appears - defaults to "off" (see BlockEffectType's own doc comment): just there from the moment the slide is, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed.

exitEffect.description: How this block disappears *before* the slide itself does - defaults to "off": never happens at all, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed - it simply stays until the slide changes.

name.description: What the author calls this block (optional): shown instead of its kind in the event graph, in the list of a page's elements and in what `weft inspect` says, and a way for tools to refer to it. Never shown to learners.

order.description: Stacking order among the blocks of its page/layout (later = on top) - see ordering.ts.

width.description: Line thickness in cqw (percent of the slide's width).

ArrowPoint.description: One waypoint of an arrow, in percent of the arrow block's own box (0,0 = its top left corner) - not necessarily within it while the arrow is being edited.

ArrowStyle.description: How an arrow is drawn: a plain line, as if drawn by hand, or in the curls of Art Nouveau.

AspectRatio.description: "W:H" - one of the presets in core/aspectRatio.ts ("16:9", "9:16", ...) or any custom pair of positive numbers, e.g. "21:9" or "1.85:1".

AudioBlock.description: A sound file: works like a video (it starts by itself or by a trigger or by the learner, it has time marks that stop it and make things appear - its events have the same ids and kinds as those of a video, see isMediaBlock) - but has no picture. On the slide it is either invisible (it only plays, started by a trigger or by `autoplay`) or has a player.

actionEffects.description: What the block does between its Aufbau and its Abbau (see ActionEffect) - in the order they were made; when they happen is a matter of the page's graph. Absent: none (a module saved before they existed).

appearance.description: "hidden": nothing to see on the slide (in the editor a small symbol marks the place); "player": the audio element's own player.

entranceEffect.description: How this block appears - defaults to "off" (see BlockEffectType's own doc comment): just there from the moment the slide is, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed.

exitEffect.description: How this block disappears *before* the slide itself does - defaults to "off": never happens at all, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed - it simply stays until the slide changes.

name.description: What the author calls this block (optional): shown instead of its kind in the event graph, in the list of a page's elements and in what `weft inspect` says, and a way for tools to refer to it. Never shown to learners.

stopPoints.description: Always kept sorted by timeSeconds - like VideoBlock.stopPoints.

BlockEffect.description: A block's own Aufbau or Abbau (see BaseBlock.entranceEffect/exitEffect below, and BlockEffectEditor in features/editor/panels/BlockPanel.tsx) - independent of the page-level Transition (core/types.ts's own Transition/TransitionType), which animates the whole slide on the way to the *next* one, not one block's own appearance within the current slide. Only the animation itself lives here - which event triggers it, and after what delay, is recorded as a TimelineEdge in PageTimeline.triggerEdges instead (see getBlockEntranceTrigger/ getBlockExitTrigger in document/pageTimeline.ts), the same single mechanism every other kind of trigger on the page uses - so this type doesn't need its own separate notion of "which event" alongside it, except for "off" (see BlockEffectType's own doc comment), which bypasses that mechanism entirely regardless of whatever trigger edge might still be stored (switching back to "none"/"fade"/"move" later picks it back up unchanged).

direction.description: "wipe" only: the way the wipe travels (an Aufbau "Nach rechts" uncovers the block from its left edge towards the right one, an Abbau covers it up the same way). Absent = "right" - optional so a module saved before it existed still loads.

durationMs.description: Only meaningful when `type` isn't "none" (which always shows/hides instantly).

motion.description: "fade" only: a small movement along with the fading. "up" / "down": the block starts a little above / below its place and settles there (an Abbau goes the same way back, off to the top / the bottom); "scale": it starts a little smaller (an Abbau shrinks). Absent: the block only fades.

moveAngle.description: "move" with "angle" only: the angle of that side in degrees, 0 to 360 - 0 is the right, 90 the bottom, 180 the left and 270 the top (the way the angle of a gradient is counted). Absent = 0.

moveDirection.description: "move" only: the side the block comes in from (an Aufbau) or goes off to (an Abbau); "angle" is the side `moveAngle` points at. Absent = "right", as it always was.

BlockEffectType.description: Every kind of appear/disappear animation a block can use for its own Aufbau (entrance) or Abbau (exit) - plus "off", which isn't an animation at all. "off": there's no Aufbau/Abbau here in the first place - the block is simply always there from the moment the slide is (for entrance) or never auto-removed (for exit); never gets a trigger of any kind (see getBlockEntranceTrigger/getBlockExitTrigger in document/pageTimeline.ts, both of which short-circuit to `null` for it), and never shows up in the page's own event graph - there's nothing there to configure or point at. "none" is a DIFFERENT thing: a real Aufbau/Abbau DOES exist, it just shows/hides instantly rather than animating - still has its own trigger (default "Weiter" for entrance), still shows up in the graph, same as "fade"/"move" do.

BlockGroup.description:
Several of a page's own blocks, bundled so they move (and resize, together, proportionally) as one unit on the canvas, same as a Keynote/PowerPoint group - see groupBlocks in document/actions.ts. Deliberately thin: no position/rotation/effect fields of its own. A group's own bounding box is always derived from its members' current positions (see resizeMath.ts's groupBoundingBox), and its "shared" Aufbau/Abbau (see GroupPanel.tsx) is UI sugar that writes the same entranceEffect/exitEffect/trigger to every member's own existing fields rather than a new, separate concept the timeline graph or the exported player need to know about - grouping is purely an editor/authoring convenience, invisible to player.runtime.js and to the data a member block carries on its own.

`blockIds` are always kept contiguous, in this exact order, within the owning Page's own block stacking order (see groupBlocks) - what lets the sidebar (PagePanel.tsx) render a clean indented bracket under one group header, and keeps "the group's own stacking position" (see bringGroupToFront/sendGroupToBack) well-defined even though there's no explicit z-index anywhere in this app (the blocks' `order` keys already double as that, see ordering.ts). Groups are page-only - a Layout has no timeline/graded state and nothing about grouping needs either, so there was no reason to extend Layout the same way.

entranceEffect.description: The Aufbau/Abbau of the group as a whole: an event of its own in the page's graph (`group-entrance:<id>`, `group-exit:<id>`), which triggers the Aufbau/Abbau of the members (explicit triggers the graph shows as one line). The members carry the same effect themselves, so the player needs nothing of the group. Absent (or "off"): the group has no effect of its own - its members are in the graph one by one.

rotation.description: Degrees, 0-360. Optional (rather than defaulting to 0 in every object literal that builds a BlockPosition) since a module saved before this field existed won't have it in its JSON either way - readers fall back to `?? 0`, so there's no real difference between "optional" and "required with a default" here, just less churn at every construction site that doesn't care about rotation.

x.description: Percent of the slide (0-100). Percent, not pixels, so the block stays put across the module's fixed aspect ratio at any render size.

BlockTranslation.description: What one block says in a language OTHER than the module's default one (see WeftModule.languages) - only the fields that have been translated; anything missing is shown in the default language's wording instead. The block's own plain fields (html, questionHtml, text, ...) ARE the default language's wording, so a module that never uses languages has none of this at all.

explanation.description: QuizBlock: the explanation shown after submitting (plain text).

items.description: ListBlock: each item's html by item id.

options.description: QuizBlock: each option's html by option id.

text.description: ButtonBlock: the label as plain text (what `html` says, without the formatting).

title.description: RevealerBlock: the heading, the text of its window and the description of its picture (`text` is its button's label).

Branch.description: A Branch only ever holds Page ids, never a LogicBlock. This is what keeps branching one level deep by construction: you cannot nest a logic block inside a branch, so the learner is always funneled back to the single main sequence after a branch ends.

condition.description: Evaluated like if/else-if/else in array order (see LogicBlock.branches): every branch but the last must carry a condition, and only the last branch may be null - it is always the unconditional "sonst" fallback taken when none of the earlier conditions matched.

pages.description: The pages of this branch, by page id; the order they're played in is each entry's own `order` (see ordering.ts) - not an array so that moving a page is a change of one field.

ButtonAppearance.description: How a button looks (ButtonBlock.appearance). Lengths are cqw (percent of the slide's width). A part that is missing is what the module's look gives it (the accent colour for the background and the border, see WeftModule.accentColor) and the defaults of DEFAULT_BUTTON_APPEARANCE (core/document/buttonAppearance.ts). The colour of the letters is part of the label.

action.description: What a click does besides being an event of the page's graph ("Button geklickt", see TimelineEventType): "advance" presses Weiter, exactly like Space/→ - everything that waits for Weiter arrives. "prev" goes back one slide (disabled on the first one). "event" does nothing of its own: what follows the click is what the graph says - by default a trigger to "Nächste Folie", which the author can change or take away (a button that only starts an animation). Once the module has ended, "advance" and "event" restart it instead. Format 4 and older had "next" here (jump to the next slide): see migrateButtonActions in io/unpack.ts.

exitEffect.description: How this block disappears *before* the slide itself does - defaults to "off": never happens at all, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed - it simply stays until the slide changes.

html.description: The label with its formatting (edited on the canvas like a text). Absent on a button that has never been formatted: `text` is its label then.

name.description: What the author calls this block (optional): shown instead of its kind in the event graph, in the list of a page's elements and in what `weft inspect` says, and a way for tools to refer to it. Never shown to learners.

onClick.description: Changes to variables that every click makes, whatever the action is (set, add, append - like the effects of a quiz).

order.description: Stacking order among the blocks of its page/layout (later = on top) - see ordering.ts.

targetPageId.description: For "goto": the page the click leads to, by id (so that the link survives pages being added, moved or removed). A page that is not there any more: the click does nothing but being an event. The sequence goes on after that page, as after a jump page.

text.description: The label as plain text - always what `html` says without its formatting, so that everything that only needs the words (the graph, a search) has them.

CheckerBlock.description: A checker: a checkbox with a text beside it - a declaration of consent, say - and under it a button "Abschicken". What happens once it is submitted depends on whether the box is ticked (`onChecked`, `onUnchecked`: changes to variables, like the effects of a quiz). It has the events of a quiz in the page's graph (a first click on the box, submitted - plain, and with the outcome: "richtig" is ticked, "falsch" is not), so that what follows can hang on them like on a quiz's, and it lives on pages only (it holds a state). It looks like the other interactive elements of the module's style (the corners and the typeface).

mustCheck.description: The box has to be ticked for "Abschicken" to be possible (an agreement that cannot be given by leaving it empty) - else it can be submitted either way, and `onUnchecked` is what a refusal does. Absent: the box need not be ticked.

name.description: What the author calls this block (optional): shown instead of its kind in the event graph, in the list of a page's elements and in what `weft inspect` says, and a way for tools to refer to it. Never shown to learners.

onChecked.description: What happens when it is submitted with the box ticked / not ticked.

required.description: A required task, as QuizBlock.required: the page cannot be left by Weiter before it has been submitted. Absent: not required.

text.description: The words beside the box (plain text, line breaks are kept).

translations.description: Other languages' wording (`text`), by locale - see BlockTranslation.

ClozeBlock.description: A gap text: a rich text in which `[[Berlin]]` is a blank (an input field in the player) whose right answer is "Berlin" (see core/document/cloze.ts), with a "Abschicken" button under it that marks which answers were right. Like a quiz it is graded, so it lives on pages only (not in a layout), and it has the same events in the page's graph (the first answer typed, submitted - plain, and right/wrong).

actionEffects.description: What the block does between its Aufbau and its Abbau (see ActionEffect) - in the order they were made; when they happen is a matter of the page's graph. Absent: none (a module saved before they existed).

answerEffects.description: What happens, in addition, for a blank whose answer is this one (keyed by what stands in the brackets).

caseSensitive.description: Whether capital and small letters have to be as written (default: they don't).

translations.description: Other languages' wording (`html`), by locale - see BlockTranslation.

CustomFont.description: A font file the user uploaded (see core/fonts/), stored as a blob keyed by `id` exactly like an AssetMeta - unlike the curated set in core/fonts/curatedFonts.ts, which ships with the app and isn't a per-document asset at all. `family` is what block HTML's font-face/font-family actually references, so renaming here would silently detach it from any text already using it.

FileEntry.description: One file offered for download by a FilesBlock. The bytes are an asset (`id`, see AssetMeta) - encrypted ones if the block is protected. The rest is plain data about the original file, and stays readable in the module whether or not there is a password.

name.description: The file's name for the download.

size.description: Size of the original file in bytes.

FilesBlock.description: Files the learners can download. With a password, the files in the archive are really encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and the learner sees them only after entering it; names, types and sizes (`files`) stay readable.

salt.description: Random salt of the key derivation (base64).

verifier.description: A known text, encrypted with the key (base64): decrypting it is how a password is checked.

Optional only so a module saved before this field existed still loads - readers fall back to DEFAULT_VIEWPORT_WIDTH (see BlockPanel.tsx).

presentationUrl.description: Optional: once revealed, show this URL instead of `url` - e.g. `url` is a live survey people join by scanning the code on their phone, this is the results view shown on screen. Falls back to `url` when empty.

qrCode.description: When true, the block shows a scannable QR code for `url` plus the plain address instead of embedding the iframe right away; clicking the address reveals the iframe, like a gate.

sandbox.description: e.g. ["allow-scripts", "allow-same-origin"] - kept explicit per block, never "allow everything" by default.

ImageEffect.description: An effect of an image (one at a time). Lengths are in cqw (percent of the slide's width).

ImageMask.description: What of an image is shown: only what is inside this closed curve (see core/runtime/imageGeometry.js). The shape it began as is only a starting point - the points can be moved, added and removed.

ImageMaskPoint.description: One point of an image's mask (a closed curve), in percent of the image block's box (0,0 = its top left corner).

radius.description: A corner is rounded by this much: the radius of the arc, in percent of the box's width. Only for a corner.

smooth.description: The curve runs smoothly through the point (else it has a corner there).

pageId.description: The page to go to (by id - the page may have been deleted since: then this way is skipped).

LinkBlock.description: A link on the slide: an element of its own (not a piece of a text) that leads to an address on the internet when it is clicked - a page, which opens in a new tab (target="_blank"). It looks like a button of the module's style (a dark grey like the window of a revealer, the corners follow the style of the interactive elements) with a globe in front of its text. It is no way to hand out a file: a browser does not save a file of another site, it only opens it - and a file that belongs to the module goes in the Files block.

ListBlock.description: A list of texts. Each item is rich text edited in place on the slide, like the options of a quiz. Its Aufbau is either the list's as a whole (the block's own `entranceEffect`, an event of the block) or - with `itemEntrance` - the same effect for every item one by one, each an event of its own in the page's graph (`list-item:<blockId>:<itemId>`, see listItemNodeId in document/pageTimeline.ts), by default one after the other on Weiter. The Abbau is always the list's as a whole.

itemEntrance.description: The Aufbau is made by each item on its own, one event per item. Only on a page (a layout has no events to trigger them).

markerAssetId.description: marker "image": the picture in front of every item.

markerColor.description: The colour of the mark - the dot, the dash or the number - as "#rrggbb"; absent or null: the colour of the text. (Not for "image": a picture has its own colours.)

markerSize.description: marker "image": the height of the picture, in em of the text (default 1.2).

name.description: What the author calls this block (optional): shown instead of its kind in the event graph, in the list of a page's elements and in what `weft inspect` says, and a way for tools to refer to it. Never shown to learners.

order.description: Stacking order among the blocks of its page/layout (later = on top) - see ordering.ts.

spacing.description: The space between two items, in cqw (percent of the slide's width - it scales with the slide, like the text does).

translations.description: Other languages' wording, by locale - see BlockTranslation.

ListItem.description: One item of a list: rich HTML, like TextBlock.html.

ListMarkerKind.description: What stands in front of the items of a ListBlock.

branches.description: Order matters - see Branch.condition for the if/else-if/else evaluation rule.

OrderKey.description: Position among the siblings of an ordered collection (a page's blocks, the page sequence, a branch's pages) - a fractional key, see core/document/ordering.ts.

groups.description: This page's own groups (see BlockGroup) - empty for the vast majority of pages, which never group anything.

jump.description: Set for a jump page (see PageJump): then the page has no blocks and is not shown.

notes.description: Notes for whoever presents the module (shown in the presenter view, see features/presenter/): plain text, in the module's default language. Only for the author: they are in the saved file and the exported .weft.zip's weft.json, but never in the module's page (index.html) or in a player file.

notesTranslations.description: The same notes in the other languages of the module, by locale; a language without an entry shows the default notes.

timeline.description: This page's timeline graph - see PageTimeline.

PageEnd.description: A "Nächste Folie" event of a page: leaving it, with `transition` (how the slide goes away - see Transition).

PageJump.description: What makes a page a jump page: it is never shown. The moment the learner gets there he is sent on to another page - the first of `targets` whose condition holds (in this order, like the branches of a logic block), else `defaultPageId` (the "sonst"). Without a default and with nothing that holds, the jump page is just passed over. The sequence goes on after the page that was jumped to, as if the learner had got there the normal way.

PageTimeline.description:
What a page's event graph stores (see docs/event-graph.md): only what does not follow from its blocks. The events themselves
- an element's Aufbau/Abbau, a video's start and stop points, what a quiz does - are derived (getPageLanes in document/pageTimeline.ts) and have stable ids made of the block's id; what is chosen by the author is here:

- `triggers`: every line of the graph, by trigger id. Keyed so that two people changing different triggers of the same page never   overwrite each other (a list that is replaced whole would). A trigger whose event or source no longer exists is pruned by   syncPageTimelineEvents.
- `ends`: the "Nächste Folie" events, by id: "end" is the page's own and always there; a quiz that goes on to the next page   after its feedback has `end:quiz:<blockId>:<richtig|falsch>`. Each has the transition of its own.

There are no implicit triggers: an Aufbau that waits for Weiter at the end of the chain has a trigger of its own, put there when the effect was chosen (see syncPageTimelineEvents), and so has "Nächste Folie". Deliberately NOT stored: the rows of the graph the editor draws (TimelineLane) - they follow entirely from the blocks and these triggers, so they are computed.

titles.description: A title the author gave an event instead of its standard one, by event id. Absent: the standard titles.

PageTrigger.description: One trigger of a page (see PageTimeline.triggers): when the event `from` has happened, the event `to` happens `delayMs` later - if `weiter`, only once the learner has pressed Weiter after `from` (then `delayMs` runs from that press). The ids are those of the page's events (see core/eventGraph and docs/event-graph.md): "start", "end" or one of document/pageTimeline.ts's `*NodeId`. An event can have several incoming triggers; any one of them is enough to make it happen.

hideOnResume.description: Legacy, from before "Video läuft weiter" was an event of its own: such a trigger (from a time mark that stops the video, to an Aufbau) is turned into the Abbau of that block, triggered by the video going on, by syncPageTimelineEvents - and the flag removed. Never written any more.

PaletteColor.description: One colour of the module's colour scheme (WeftModule.colorPalette): "#rrggbb".

PlaceholderBlock.description: A placeholder for a text on the pages that use a layout (only exists in a layout): it has no text of its own. What the author sets up is where it stands and how its text looks; the `html` is a sample that carries that formatting (font, size, colour, alignment, ...) - it is never shown on a page. On a page the slot can be clicked to type a text, which then starts out formatted like the sample (see core/document/placeholders.ts).

actionEffects.description: What the block does between its Aufbau and its Abbau (see ActionEffect) - in the order they were made; when they happen is a matter of the page's graph. Absent: none (a module saved before they existed).

entranceEffect.description: How this block appears - defaults to "off" (see BlockEffectType's own doc comment): just there from the moment the slide is, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed.

exitEffect.description: How this block disappears *before* the slide itself does - defaults to "off": never happens at all, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed - it simply stays until the slide changes.

html.description: A sample text that has the formatting (the author edits and formats it like any text).

label.description: What it is for ("Titel", "Untertitel", ...): shown in the slot on the pages.

name.description: What the author calls this block (optional): shown instead of its kind in the event graph, in the list of a page's elements and in what `weft inspect` says, and a way for tools to refer to it. Never shown to learners.

order.description: Stacking order among the blocks of its page/layout (later = on top) - see ordering.ts.

ProgressBlock.description: A progress bar: a track with a fill that is as long as the value of a variable says (0 to 100 - what is below or above is held to that). By default the variable is `progress`, the virtual one that tells how far the learner is through the module; any other number (or computed) variable can be shown as well. It works on a layout too, and is the same bar on every slide that has it: after a change of slide the slide changes first, then the variable has its new value, and then the fill moves - if `animate` is on, so does it after every change of the variable.

animate.description: Whether the fill moves to a new value instead of jumping there.

trackColor.description: The colour of the track behind it.

variable.description: The name of the variable the bar shows.

explanation.description: What is told after submitting, under the "right" / "wrong": an explanation of the answer (plain text, lines are kept; translations in BlockTranslation.explanation). Absent or empty: nothing.

name.description: What the author calls this block (optional): shown instead of its kind in the event graph, in the list of a page's elements and in what `weft inspect` says, and a way for tools to refer to it. Never shown to learners.

onCorrect.description: What happens once the quiz as a whole was answered right / wrong (all options as they should be / not).

open.description: An open question rather than a test: nothing is right or wrong. Submitting it is thanked ("Danke!") instead of judged, correctOptionIds and onIncorrect are ignored, onCorrect is what happens on submitting (and it counts as "richtig" for the page's graph), and an answer's own effects are by whether it is ticked (onRight) or not (onWrong). Optional: a module saved before this is a test.

order.description: Stacking order among the blocks of its page/layout (later = on top) - see ordering.ts.

questionHtml.description: Rich HTML, exactly like TextBlock.html - edited in place on the canvas with the same bold/italic/underline/font/size/color toolbar (see EditableText/TextEditor). A module saved before this held HTML is migrated on load (see unpack.ts) by escaping its old plain text into an equivalent paragraph, so every reader can assume this is always already-safe HTML.

required.description: A required task ("Pflichtaufgabe"): a Weiter that would leave the page - the Weiter button, Space, the arrow, a tap - is held back until it has been submitted, and a button whose action is "Weiter" is greyed out meanwhile (see weiter in player.runtime.js). Absent: not required.

QuizOption.description: One answer of a quiz. An option is "handled right" when it is ticked if it is a correct one and left alone if it isn't (so even knowing that an answer is wrong earns something); "handled wrong" is the opposite. Each case can have effects of its own (points of one kind or another, minus points ...), independent of the quiz as a whole being right. Optional so that a module saved before they existed loads as it is: no effects.

RevealerBlock.description: A small icon in a coloured shape on the slide. A click on it (or an incoming trigger of its event, see TimelineEventType "revealer-open") opens a window around it with a heading and - all of them optional - a small text, a picture and a button; the window closes with its x. The sign on the icon is black or white, whichever stands out more from `color`.

actionEffects.description: What the block does between its Aufbau and its Abbau (see ActionEffect) - in the order they were made; when they happen is a matter of the page's graph. Absent: none (a module saved before they existed).

body.description: The small text of the window (plain text, with line breaks); "" for none.

button.description: The button of the window, or null for none.

color.description: The colour of the icon (a hex colour).

entranceEffect.description: How this block appears - defaults to "off" (see BlockEffectType's own doc comment): just there from the moment the slide is, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed.

exitEffect.description: How this block disappears *before* the slide itself does - defaults to "off": never happens at all, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed - it simply stays until the slide changes.

imageAlt.description: The description of the picture for those who cannot see it.

imageAssetId.description: The picture of the window (an asset), or null for none.

name.description: What the author calls this block (optional): shown instead of its kind in the event graph, in the list of a page's elements and in what `weft inspect` says, and a way for tools to refer to it. Never shown to learners.

order.description: Stacking order among the blocks of its page/layout (later = on top) - see ordering.ts.

windowStyle.description: The look of the window: dark (the default) or light.

RevealerButton.description: The button in the window of a Revealer: what a click does is what ButtonBlock.action says (without the picking of a plain "next slide": "event" is "what the graph says after `revealer-button:<id>`").

onClick.description: Changes to variables that every click makes.

RevealerIcon.description: The icons of a Revealer: an i, an exclamation mark in a triangle, an exclamation mark in a circle, a question mark.

ScriptBlock.description: A logic block (kind "script"): some JavaScript the page runs when the block's event of the page's graph is reached (see scriptRunNodeId in document/pageTimeline.ts) - a green event that, like the Aufbau of any block, is triggered by Weiter by default and can be triggered by anything else. In the editor it is a hexagon with a gear on the slide; the player shows nothing. The code has `vars` (read and write the module's variables by name), `debug(...)`, `trigger(name)` (an event of the page, by its title), `jump(slide, transition, options)` and `VanillaLM`; whoever writes it has to know what they do (see runScript in player.runtime.js). A page's block only - there are no events on a layout. What the module's script libraries (WeftModule.scriptLibraries) define is there too.

ScriptLibrary.description: A JavaScript library (the text of a .js file) for the logic blocks of the module: it is run once when the module starts - in the order of WeftModule.scriptLibraries, in the global scope, before any logic block's code - so what it defines (a function, an object on `window`, a top-level `const`) can be used by the code of every logic block. It belongs to the module, not to a block: deleting a logic block does not delete it.

code.description: The code, as it was in the file.

fileName.description: The name of the file it came from ("mylib.js"): what it is called in the lists. Unique in the module.

SequenceEntry.description: One entry of WeftModule.sequence: a node plus its position in the main sequence.

blurBehind.description: Blur what is behind the shape (frosted glass): only for a rectangle or an ellipse. See backdropBlur.ts.

starInnerRadius.description: Only meaningful for "star" - how far in the star's inner vertices sit, 0-100 percent of the outer radius; 100 would collapse it into a regular (starPoints*2)-gon.

ShapeCornerRadii.description: One rounding value per corner of a "rectangle" ShapeBlock - each 0 (sharp) to 50 (fully rounded/pill-shaped at that corner), as a percent of the block's own shorter *true* on-slide side (its actual rendered width vs height, accounting for both the slide's own aspect ratio and the block's own on-slide width/height - see ShapeSvg.tsx's roundedRectPath) - not of the abstract 0-100 square every shape is drawn in before being stretched to the block's own shape. That distinction is what keeps a corner a true circular arc rather than turning elliptical the moment the block itself isn't square, matching what "rounded rectangle" means in PowerPoint/ Keynote (which only ever expose one shared radius via a single handle - ShapeEditor in panels/BlockPanel.tsx additionally lets all four be set independently).

ShapeFill.description: A shape's own fill - "none" (see-through, stroke-only), a flat color, or a gradient. Only the fields matching `type` are actually read when rendering; the others still round-trip in the document so switching the fill type back and forth in the editor never loses whatever was last configured on the side that isn't currently showing.

angle.description: Degrees, only meaningful for "linear" - 0 points right, 90 points down, matching BlockPosition.rotation's own clockwise-from-horizontal convention.

stops.description: At least two - see GradientStopsEditor in panels/BlockPanel.tsx, which never lets the count drop below that (a one-stop gradient isn't a gradient). Not required to be sorted by offset; SVG/CSS both render stops in list order regardless of their own offset values.

ShapeKind.description: The basic PowerPoint/Keynote-style shapes ShapeBlock supports - "polygon" is any regular n-gon (ShapeBlock.sides picks n), not a free-form outline; there's no path editor.

blur.description: cqw, all three - see ShapeStroke.width's own doc comment for why.

width.description: cqw (percent of the slide's own rendered width - the same unit block text is sized in, see App.css's .weft-edit-block) rather than a plain pixel count, so a stroke's visual weight stays constant when this particular shape is resized (matching how a PowerPoint line weight doesn't stretch along with the shape) while still scaling along with everything else when the whole slide is displayed larger or smaller (e.g. presenting on a projector).

StaticBlock.description:
Blocks a Layout may contain. Quiz (or any future graded/interactive block) is deliberately excluded here: a Layout is a page template, and templates must not carry graded state. A navigation button (or a shape, which carries no state at all) has nothing graded to exclude, so
- unlike Quiz - both are allowed in a Layout, letting an author bake e.g. one consistent background shape or "Weiter" button into every slide of that layout.

TexBlock.description: A TeX formula (rendered with KaTeX in display mode, so it may span several lines via a double backslash). Behaves like an image on the slide: it is scaled to fit its box (contain), so resizing the box resizes the formula. Formatting is deliberately limited to the block as a whole (`color`) plus whatever TeX commands the author writes into `tex` itself (e.g. a color command around part of it).

color.description: CSS color for the whole formula; "" = inherit the slide's own text color.

box.description: A background and border behind the text - a card, in one block (instead of a shape under a text, which is two blocks, one Aufbau each, to keep together when copying). Absent: none, as every text before this existed.

placeholderOf.description: Set on a text a page has for a placeholder of its layout (see PlaceholderBlock): the id of that layout block. The text is the page's own - it can be edited and formatted like any text - but where it stands is the placeholder's, and "reset" brings back the placeholder's formatting. When the layout has no such placeholder any more (another layout was chosen, it was removed) it is a plain text.

scrollable.description: Text longer than the block can be scrolled vertically (never horizontally). Off by default - and absent on every block saved before this existed, which therefore stay unscrollable: the overflowing text is simply cut off at the block's edge.

translations.description: Other languages' wording, by locale ("fr_FR") - see BlockTranslation.

TextBox.description: The background and border of a text block (TextBlock.box). Colours are "#rrggbb"; lengths are cqw (percent of the slide's width).

blur.description: Blur what is behind the block (CSS backdrop-filter): the background shows through, out of focus - frosted glass. See backdropBlur.ts.

borderColor.description: The colour of the border; null: none.

padding.description: The room between the border and the text.

background.description: "wheel" only: what is behind the swinging slides. Absent = the plain background of the player (black).

contentOnly.description: "move" only: slide just the page's own content while the slide itself (background and the layout's blocks) stays put - possible only when the next slide uses the same layout, otherwise the whole slide moves regardless (with the content trailing it by a few ms).

direction.description: "move", "cube" and "wheel" (left or right only) only. Absent = that type's default (see defaultDirection in document/transitions.ts) - every option below is optional so a module saved before it existed still loads.

durationMs.description: Only meaningful when type isn't "none" - how long the animation takes, in milliseconds. Defaults to 500 (see setPageTransition/setPageTransitionDuration in document/actions.ts).

hardEdge.description: "iris" only: a hard-edged circle instead of the default soft one.

irisCenter.description: "iris" only: where the circle opens from, in percent of the slide. Absent = the middle.

TransitionBackground.description: What is behind the slides while a "wheel" turns: a colour or a picture (an asset of the module).

TransitionDirection.description: Which way the OUTGOING slide travels (a Move slides it off that way, a Cube turns that way) - the incoming one arrives from the opposite side.

TransitionType.description: Every kind of transition Weft knows how to animate the move to the *next* node with - "none" is an instant cut, all others are animated (see player.runtime.js's animateTransition). Kept as its own type rather than inlined into Transition so the player and the editor's own options list (see document/transitions.ts) can both reference just this.

expression.description: The formula of a "computed" variable; absent on every other type.

fixed.description: A built-in variable (`success`): always present, never renamed or removed, and a Ja/Nein either way - its type can only be switched between "boolean" (set by hand/quiz effects) and "computed" (a formula, whose result is read as Ja/Nein). See ensureBuiltinVariables in core/document/variables.ts.

VariableType.description: "computed" is a variable whose value is never stored: it is worked out from other variables by its `expression` every time it is read (see core/document/expressions.ts for the language).

actionEffects.description: What the block does between its Aufbau and its Abbau (see ActionEffect) - in the order they were made; when they happen is a matter of the page's graph. Absent: none (a module saved before they existed).

entranceEffect.description: How this block appears - defaults to "off" (see BlockEffectType's own doc comment): just there from the moment the slide is, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed.

exitEffect.description: How this block disappears *before* the slide itself does - defaults to "off": never happens at all, i.e. exactly how every block behaved before this field existed - it simply stays until the slide changes.

muted.description: Autoplay only ever actually starts when this is true too (every browser's autoplay policy requires it) - BlockPanel.tsx keeps the two in sync in the UI so that's never a silent trap.

name.description: What the author calls this block (optional): shown instead of its kind in the event graph, in the list of a page's elements and in what `weft inspect` says, and a way for tools to refer to it. Never shown to learners.

order.description: Stacking order among the blocks of its page/layout (later = on top) - see ordering.ts.

stopPoints.description: Always kept sorted by timeSeconds (see VideoStopPointDialog) - so both the dialog's own mini-timeline and any future reader can assume ascending order rather than re-sorting.

VideoStopPoint.description: A point on a video's own timeline - an event and a trigger at once (see VideoStopPointDialog in panels/BlockPanel.tsx): something is meant to happen once playback reaches it, though what isn't modeled yet beyond stopsVideo.

stopsVideo.description: Whether reaching this point actually pauses the video (the "Video hier stoppen" checkbox in VideoStopPointDialog) - off just marks the moment without interrupting playback. Defaults to true, since pausing is the only thing a stop point can actually do today.

timeSeconds.description: Seconds into the video's own playback.

WeftFileJson.description: What weft.json in a .weft file holds, and what docs/weft.schema.json describes (generated from this type: `npm run schema`). Other tools - the command line tool in cli/, or a program that builds a module - read and write exactly this.

accentColor.description: The accent colour "#rrggbb" of the standard elements: the buttons (a button block that has no colour of its own, a quiz's submit button) and what marks a chosen answer. Everything else of theirs (border, hover, tints) follows from it and from `brightness`. Missing: the blue of the quiz's submit button (a module saved before this existed had dark buttons - they are blue now, like the quiz's).

brightness.description: Whether the slides have a light or a dark background, by and large (the module's settings, "Aussehen"): the plain slide, its standard text and the standard elements - quiz, cloze, button, language switch, files - are styled to suit it. Missing: "light".

colorPalette.description: The module's colour scheme: colours that come up again and again, managed under the module's settings and offered in every colour picker (features/editor/ColorField.tsx). Missing in modules saved before this existed - read it as empty. A block that uses one of them just carries the hex value, so changing a scheme colour later does not recolour what already uses it.

coverAssetId.description: The cover picture that stands for the module (the start screen's tiles, ...): the id of an asset (a PNG - the upload is turned into one). In a saved or exported file it is the file `logo.png` at the top (not in assets/), see packDocument. Without one the file gets a picture of the first slide there instead (core/io/coverImage.ts).

id.description: Set once with crypto.randomUUID() at creation and never reused, so an LMS can key progress on it forever.

interactiveStyle.description: How the buttons and the answers of a quiz look (the module's settings, "Aussehen"), apart from their colours: "plain" (missing: as they have always been), "elegant" (a serif face), "round" (pill-shaped), "futuristic" (angular, two corners cut, a technical face). Each also has its own, subtle look for when the pointer is over a clickable element.

keyboardNavigationEnabled.description: On by default (matches every module saved before this existed - see unpack.ts's migration). Switched off, the player ignores Space/←/→ entirely - only an author-placed button block or a quiz's own onCorrect/onIncorrect effects can move the learner forward or back. The main reason to turn it off: without it, nothing stops a learner from pressing ← to back up past a quiz they've already answered and retake it.

languages.description: The languages this module is offered in, as locales ("de_DE", "en_US" - see core/i18n/languages.ts), the first being the default one. Empty (the default) means a single-language module: no `userlanguage` variable, no language switchers, nothing translated.

scriptLibraries.description: JavaScript libraries the logic blocks can use (see ScriptLibrary). Absent: none.

sequence.description: The main sequence, by the id of the page / logic block each entry stands for; played in each entry's own `order` (see ordering.ts's orderedValues, and sequenceOf in document/sequence.ts).

template.description: A template or an example that ships with Weft (or is passed on to be started from): opening it makes a copy of its own - a new id, no file, not yet saved anywhere, so it has to be given a place first - and that copy is not a template. The file itself is never changed by working on it. Absent or false: an ordinary module.
